visual.label: Northbridge FC's share of the ball

scenes.narration: Northbridge had just 38 percent of the ball. Harbour City took 17 shots. And Northbridge still won 2 to 1. So how do you win a match you barely touch the ball in?
In the next few minutes you will see three keys behind this result: quality over volume, accuracy when it mattered, and timing. By the end you will spot them in your next match.
First, the picture. Northbridge lined up in a 4-4-2. Harbour City in a 4-3-3. Harbour City scored first, in the 23rd minute, through A. Moreno. Northbridge answered after the break.

Key one: quality over volume. Harbour City had 8 more shots, but Northbridge created more expected goals, 1.42 against 1.10. The numbers suggest Northbridge's chances came from better positions. Recap: it is not how many shots, it is how good they are. If this helps you read the game, subscribe.

Key two: accuracy. Northbridge put 5 of their 9 shots on target. Harbour City managed 4 from 17. Harbour City also had 8 corners to Northbridge's 3, yet those set pieces brought no goal. Recap: be clinical when the chance comes.

Key three: timing. J. Okafor equalised in the 51st minute, early in the second half. Then in the 78th minute Okafor turned provider, setting up L. Brandt for the winner. Recap: one sharp spell can decide a match.
So what can a player or coach take from this? Value the quality of a chance over the number of shots. Make your attempts count. And stay ready, because matches often turn in short spells.
How do you win with 38 percent of the ball? Make better chances and finish them. That is how Northbridge did it. See you in the next breakdown.
